A monolithic architecture is a software architecture where a single unit or module is used to represent the entire application. In a monolithic architecture, the entire application is built as one unit, and all the components are tightly coupled. This means that if there is a problem in one part of the application, the entire application has to be restarted or updated. On the other hand, A microservices architecture is a software architecture that structures an application as a collection of small, independent units called services. Each service is a separate entity and they are loosely coupled. If there is a problem in one service, only that service needs to be restarted or updated.
